Subject: DPA redline playbook & ops handoff — DataHealth

Team —

DataHealth sent through a consolidated redline this morning (attached). They’ve pushed a couple of non-standard asks we need to triage:

- Expanded processor role language (they want explicit subprocessor approval workflow)
- SCCs: they insist on a specific routing to EU-only nodes + an audit of Azure region fallbacks
- KMS/HSM: request for proof of customer-key rotation support and a one-off attestation

Immediate asks:
1) Legal (Laura): can you take the redline and mark must-not-accept vs negotiable items? There are a few proposed indemnity and liability tweaks that look bigger than normal.
2) Privacy (Karthik): please validate the SCCs mapping XLS I started (attached) — confirm whether our fallback behavior to nearest-region compute will trigger a transfer under their interpretation.
3) Sales/Ops (Ben): we need an operations-runbook style handoff for the on-call and escalation lane if we require emergency cross-region failover. Can you sketch an initial ops checklist and identify whether Dedicated/Private offerings change the ask?

Timeline: DataHealth asked for a response by next Wednesday 10/27 EOD CET. I’ve attached the redline v3 and an initial SCCs mapping workbook.

Attachments: DataHealth_DPA_redline_v3.docx, SCCs_region_mapping.xlsx

Thanks —
Naomi

Thanks Ben / Naomi —

We can do 10/22 at 15:00 CET. The procurement team wants the annex because their regulators require explicit routing commitments and remediation steps if data moves for less than 24 hours. Regarding subprocessors: we are open to a narrow delegated approval process (e.g., notify + 5 business day escalation window) rather than pre-approval for every subprocessor.

From our perspective, the key deliverables are:
- An annex describing primary EU-routing and the exact failure modes that would trigger fallback to non-EU regions
- An operational contact list and a simple runbook for emergency region pinning
- A three-item attestation clause for KMS support (rotate keys, customer-managed keys, HSM integration)

I’ve attached an internal checklist we used on a prior deal for reference (not shared here). We will review Redwood’s draft annex and revert next week.

Best,
Elena

Head of Security Programs

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Oct 2026 08:27:00 -0700
Subject: RE: DPA redline playbook & ops handoff — DataHealth

Thanks for the heads-up. I reviewed the redline and sketched an issue list (high-level):

1) Indemnity & liability: They propose a reverse-liability carveout tied to routing failures. Must push back — liability tied to routing policy will create exposure we don’t accept without limits. Recommend adding an explicit mitigation ladder instead (annex + capped liability for transfer events).
2) Subprocessor approval: Acceptable compromise is a notify-and-escalate process (notify within 5 business days, customer may object within 10 business days, escalation to legal for unresolved objections) — that maps to previous precedent.
3) SCCs / transfer-impact: We need a short transfer-impact addendum that references the SCCs used and documents the minimal set of circumstances that constitute a cross-border transfer (e.g., KV-cache hotshard movement, manual failover, maintenance window >2 hours). Karthik — please confirm the technical triggers.
4) KMS/HSM attestation: We can provide a statement of supported features and logs (rotation capability, customer-managed key options) but cannot provide a one-off attestation executed by engineering. We should propose a standard security questionnaire response + architecture diagram.

I’ll inline redline language and send a tracked-change DPA annex by EOD 10/23. If Ops (Ben) can provide the runbook and on-call contacts, I’ll incorporate references to the operational checklist and the escalation ladder.

—Laura
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Privacy
Redwood Inference
